chunks: 3859 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurarah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Samurah ibn Jundab had a date cluster in the orchard of a man from the Ansar, and the residence of the Ansari contained the path to the orchard. He would come to it and enter upon him without seeking permission. So he said: You come and enter while we are in a condition in which we dislike that you see us. So when you come, seek permission so that we may guard ourselves, then permit you and you may enter. He said: I will not do that; it is my property, I enter upon it and do not seek permission.

Then the Ansari went to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and complained to him and informed him. So he sent for Samurah, and he came. He said to him: Seek permission before entering upon him. But he refused and said to him the like of what he had said to the Ansari. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم offered to buy it from him for a price, but he refused. And he kept increasing for him, yet he refused to sell. So when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم saw that, he said to him: You shall have a date cluster in Paradise. But he refused to accept that.
Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered the Ansari to uproot the palm tree and throw it to him, and he said: There is no harm and no causing of harm.

key_terms.إِضْرَارَ: reciprocal or deliberate causing of harm
key_terms.بِٱلثَّمَنِ: for a price or payment in purchase
key_terms.عَذْقٌ: a date cluster or palm possession held by Samurah in the orchard
key_terms.لَا ضَرَرَ: no harm is to be inflicted
key_terms.ٱلْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, offered here as compensation in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith 'There is no harm and no causing of harm' in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the case of Samurah ibn Jundab, whose insistence on accessing his property without permission caused harm and intrusion upon an Ansari household. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم attempted reconciliation through instruction and compensation, and when this was refused, he removed the basis of harm and stated the principle: 'There is no harm and no causing of harm.' This report is foundational in Shia fiqh for legal reasoning about preventing harm and protecting the rights of others.
